climate_pressure: Rainfall variability, dry spells and rising temperatures.
documented_impact: Pressure on rainfed and pastoral livelihood strategies and adaptation choices.
fcv_mediator: Cultivation encroachment, livestock mobility, access to wells/pasture, demographic pressure and weak/unequal land-governance implementation.
possible_consequence: Localized disputes or violence between resource users may become more likely where institutions fail to manage competing access.
geographies: particularly pastoral/agropastoral contexts in Tahoua and Tillabéri
resilience_factors: protected mobility corridors and equitable water/pasture rules
compact_statement: Climate stress can alter livelihood strategies, but whether this becomes conflict depends strongly on land institutions, access rules and political-economic conditions. (ResearchGate)

documented_impact: Livelihood losses; 2025 flooding affected livelihoods of about 474,000 people.
fcv_mediator: Existing conflict exposure, displacement and restricted humanitarian access.
possible_consequence: Flood-affected conflict zones may face deeper food-security or recovery problems than equally flooded but accessible areas.
geographies: with special relevance to conflict-affected areas
uncertainty: No counterfactual estimate of the added effect of conflict on flood recovery.
compact_statement: Flood risk and insecurity can compound because conflict changes access to assistance and recovery capacity rather than because flooding itself causes violence. (FAOHome)

documented_impact: Changing pastoral mobility and water/pasture strategies.
fcv_mediator: Agricultural encroachment, corridor obstruction, well access, unequal legal representation and weak Rural Code enforcement.
possible_consequence: Conflict risk may increase at specific encounter points between mobile herders and cultivators.
uncertainty: Present-day magnitude and geographic distribution are not established.
resilience_factors: Legally protected corridors and credible local mediation
compact_statement: Water or pasture scarcity is not sufficient to produce violence; conflict emerges through contested access and governance. (ResearchGate)

climate_pressure: Background rainfall variability and agricultural climate dependence.
documented_impact: Civil insecurity restricted access to fields and caused localized production shortfalls in Tillabéri and Diffa in 2025.
possible_consequence: Households with reduced farm access may possess less income, stocks and flexibility to absorb subsequent drought/flood shocks.
uncertainty: Household-level resilience losses are not quantified.
compact_statement: Current evidence more clearly demonstrates insecurity constraining climate-sensitive livelihoods than climate shocks directly causing insecurity. (FAOHome)

climate_pressure: Floods, droughts and other covariate shocks remain background risks.
documented_impact: Displacement and insecurity increase needs while health, education and other services face access and funding constraints.
fcv_mediator: Forced displacement, insecure roads/territories, concentrated urban demand and resource constraints.
possible_consequence: Reduced baseline service capacity may make subsequent climate emergencies harder to absorb.
alternative_explanations: rapid population growth and fiscal constraints
uncertainty: Direct climate-adaptation outcome evaluation is absent.
compact_statement: FCV can erode the service base on which effective disaster response and adaptation depend.

documented_impact: Farmers and pastoralists diversify, change mobility, intensify agriculture, build wells or monetize previously shared resources.
fcv_mediator: Unequal capital, tenure, access and institutional representation.
possible_consequence: Some adaptation choices may shift costs or exclude other groups, creating grievances or disputes.
geographies: Local rural Niger in older field evidence
alternative_explanations: Commercialization and demographic growth independent of climate
resilience_factors: participatory governance and conflict-sensitive adaptation design
compact_statement: An adaptation intervention should not be assumed peace-positive merely because it reduces climate exposure. (ResearchGate)

documented_impact: Niger's policies call for improved forecasting, early warning and locally accessible climate services; UNICEF reports anticipatory flood preparation.
fcv_mediator: Timeliness and inclusiveness of information/assistance, local capacity and financing.
possible_consequence: Earlier action could reduce livelihood losses and pressure on crisis-response systems, provided services reach insecure and marginalized communities.
alternative_explanations: market access and infrastructure may dominate household outcomes
uncertainty: Current programme descriptions do not establish avoided losses or peace effects.
compact_statement: Early warning is a plausible resilience mechanism, but current evidence in this packet mostly demonstrates capacity and outputs rather than impacts.

climate_pressure: Climate variability raises the value of flexible access to land, pasture and water.
documented_impact: Resource-access disputes occur where mobility and cultivation overlap.
fcv_mediator: Quality and legitimacy of local dispute-resolution institutions.
possible_consequence: Inclusive land commissions and customary/formal mediation may reduce escalation.
geographies: broader mechanisms referenced in the 2026 World Bank diagnostic
alternative_explanations: local power relations and enforcement capacity
uncertainty: Louma finding is old and one-community evidence.
resilience_factors: Representation of both livelihood groups and women
compact_statement: Peace-supporting capacity appears to depend less on resource abundance alone than on legitimate institutions governing access and disputes. (ResearchGate) ---
